helpData.changelog.v0_8_10.text: Adoption terminology: adopted into the family / adopted out.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_17.text: Surrogate and gestational carrier representation adjusted to the 2025 correction.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_24.text: Relationship menu supports ended and consanguineous statuses together.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_35.text: Intergenerational couples represented by a direct diagonal.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_40.text: Click-to-open tooltip with direct access to Clinical and genetic information.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_41.text: Consultand shortcut in the tooltip (arrow + C).
helpData.changelog.v0_8_43.text: Full-width interface: the permanent sidebar is removed and the add form moves below the legend and above Pedigree conditions.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_44.text: Usability: the application uses 90% of the width, Conditions appear below family details, shortcuts are centered in their own card above the viewer, and the individual form occupies one row.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_45.text: Add individual, Advanced relationships and Lists are aligned on one desktop row; dropdowns are adjusted for their new widths.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_46.text: The Add individual form redistributes its main fields across two rows and centers the Add button.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_47.text: Quick statuses in Add individual are centered and shortcuts are added for male/female consultands and couples with one son or daughter.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_48.text: Adding parents to a generation-I individual inserts a new generation I and shifts the entire previous pedigree down one generation.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_49.text: Main actions move from the header to a card to the right of the quick-add shortcuts. The quick-add card no longer has a visible heading.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_50.text: Clinical and genetic information is available for all pedigree record types. SAB, TOP and ECT also support condition-specific statuses and clinical representation.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_51.text: Clinical and genetic information moves to an overlay side panel on the right. The pedigree remains visible and the page does not scroll when the panel opens or closes.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_52.text: The clinical panel keeps the selected record visible and provides Previous/Next navigation following visual pedigree order.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_53.text: The tooltip is reorganized into an operational record with separate sections for Status, Clinical information, Add relative, Clinical summary, More options and Edit/Delete.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_54.text: Scrolling reveals a compact bar with Undo, Redo, Save and Back to pedigree, which disappears on returning to the main actions.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_55.text: Add individual, Advanced relationships and Lists act as an accordion. Ctrl/Cmd+S, F, +/− and Esc are added as global shortcuts, alongside Ctrl/Cmd+Z/Y for Undo/Redo.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_56.text: Regular confirmations are now shown as toasts, and a sequential clinical-review mode tracks progress and timestamps of reviewed records.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_57.text: The three management cards start collapsed; checkbox/symbol alignment was fixed, quick additions center the pedigree, reviews are overall and persistent, and action icons stay on one row.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_58.text: The same button marks or cancels overall review. The case selector shows Reviewed/Not reviewed, and creation shortcuts are compacted into one row.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_59.text: Marking or cancelling review saves the case automatically. Quick-add shortcuts scroll to and center the pedigree. Saved cases now include All/Reviewed/Not reviewed quick filters.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_60.text: Validate pedigree button: QC independent of professional review, with errors, warnings and information linked to individuals and Bennett/NSGC references; validation does not change or save data.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_61.text: QC expanded to six domains: structure, family, Bennett/NSGC, clinical/genetic, documentation and graphical representation (including SVG geometry). Compact QC indicator. New reviews preserve content signatures to detect later changes; these are not electronic signatures or clinical validation.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_62.text: Live QC recalculates automatically when people, relationships, conditions or family data change; the four-light indicator uses red for errors, amber for warnings, blue for information and green for no issues, with purple for graphical issues. Details open only when the indicator or summary is clicked. Professional review remains independent.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_63.text: Single-light QC pilot: gray, red, amber, blue or green according to live automated results. The family ID column is wider and save/review/QC badges wrap without overlapping; indication and comments begin farther right. The issues panel stays closed by default.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_64.text: QC issues identify records by pedigree number (I-1, II-3…) and name rather than internal UIDs, even if numbering is hidden in the drawing. The review button is amber when pending and green when reviewed. Hover icons no longer clip at the top, while animation is preserved.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_65.text: T25: for multiple unions, the descendant axis of a routed couple is chosen from its own offspring positions within a free corridor. This prevents a third union from sharing the second union’s descendant axis and confusing sibships. Family structure, numbering, QC and exports are unchanged. Two T25a/T25b test examples are included.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_66.text: Independent intended parentage: up to two intended parents can be selected in Advanced options of an offspring or pregnancy without adding genetic parentage lines. Automatic annotation uses current pedigree numbers in SVG, PNG and PDF. Intended parentage is not inferred from couples or donors. New optional intended_parent_uids field (JSON 4.13). PedigrAPP documentation convention, not a standardized Bennett symbol.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_67.text: Horizontal mouse dragging of individuals preserves record clicks, recalculates connectors and row spacing while dragging, stores offsets in JSON 4.14 and supports Undo/Redo. ↺ resets horizontal adjustments only. Dragging does not change generation or genealogical order.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_68.text: Reproductive representation: sperm donors, egg donors and external gestational carriers are placed near the recipient couple when identifiable, making room among siblings instead of placing them at the end of the sibship. Double donation plus G is treated as a contiguous block, with the pregnancy below the person carrying it. If recipients cannot be identified, the previous layout is retained. No new biological links or JSON changes.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_69.text: New Add relative shortcuts from the record: fetus P with unknown sex by default, sperm donor D and egg donor D linked directly to the selected outcome. Fetus and stillbirth now support quick sex changes (unknown/male/female). In the new record form, an egg donor initially has woman gender and female sex assigned at birth, both editable. No fictional couple is added for donors.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_70.text: Added a quick Father, mother and fetus template (P, sex unknown), alongside son/daughter templates. It also serves as a basic prenatal case without assuming a clinical indication, affected status or gestational age. The record supports adding a fetus as offspring of a couple; with multiple unions, an explicit partner selector prevents assignment to the wrong parent. JSON schema and Bennett symbols are unchanged.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_71.text: Removed the partner dropdown when adding a fetus from a person with multiple unions. The Fetus shortcut remains available, initially linked only to the selected individual; any second parentage can be specified later where appropriate. No changes to the prenatal template or data schema.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_72.text: Original ⇄ mode for reordering siblings within their sibship (extended in 0.8.73).
helpData.changelog.v0_8_73.text: The ⇄ mode allows any individual to be reordered freely within their generation, including across sibships and donors. Couples/twins move as blocks without changing birth data or relationships. Ordering is persistent and supports Undo/Redo and ↺.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_74.text: Clicking a couple line now lets users set No children (by choice/unspecified reason) or Infertility. Attribution and an optional reason use the same fields and validation as Advanced relationships. Standard Undo/Redo and saving remain available.
helpData.changelog.v0_8_75.text: Under Add relative, an individual’s record now has reproductive-status shortcuts: a single bar for No children (by choice/unspecified reason) and two bars for Infertility. They apply to the selected person, not their partner, show the active state and can be toggled off. Reasons remain editable under Advanced options. Donors, gestational carriers, fetuses, stillbirths, SAB/TOP/ECT and multiple-individual groups are excluded; No children cannot be set when offspring are already recorded. JSON 4.16 is unchanged.
helpData.changelog.v1_0_0.text: First public version without institutional branding: simplified application header, PDF without institutional letterheads or corporate logos, and documentation suitable for public distribution. JSON format, layout and clinical rules remain unchanged.
helpData.changelog.v1_0_1.text: Legal, documentation and metadata update only: EUPL-1.2, registered authorship, clinical/scientific team and Safe Creative registration. No changes to functionality, QC, layout, exports or JSON schema 4.16.
helpData.changelog.v1_0_2.text: Documentation and publication metadata only: Zenodo DOI and citation metadata. No changes to functionality, QC, layout, exports or JSON schema 4.16.
helpData.changelog.v1_0_3.text: New Stillbirth (SB) shortcut under Add relative: creates offspring with unknown sex by default, the stillbirth symbol, and automatic parentage to the unambiguous couple. With multiple unions, only the selected parent is linked. Undo/Redo, sex editing, and JSON schema 4.16 remain unchanged.
helpData.changelog.v1_0_4.text: The PDF report header now includes the original PedigrAPP logo embedded in the document so it prints correctly. Exporting to PDF preserves the button icon without leaving a permanent text label. JSON schema 4.16 is unchanged.
helpData.changelog.v1_0_5.text: Version 1.0.5 adds bilingual English/Spanish UI, help, QC, and PDF reports. Switching languages preserves family data, clinical annotations, and layout geometry. The rc8 functionality is retained and repository documentation is now available in English.
helpData.changelog.v1_0_5_rc3.text: ES/EN prototype expanded: editor messages and validations migrated to semantic keys, help history translated, and stable keys for symbols and release versions. The i18n regression gate prevents new unreviewed literals. No changes to JSON schema or pedigree geometry.
helpData.changelog.v1_0_5_rc4.text: Bilingual startup without language flash: the ES/EN catalogs are built from JSON and loaded before the editor. Generated catalogs are checked against the canonical translations. No changes to data or pedigree geometry.
helpData.changelog.v1_0_5_rc5.text: Translated toolbar tooltips, condition editing, and the clinical and genetic information panel; user-entered data is unchanged.
helpData.changelog.v1_0_5_rc6.text: Translated condition legend text, empty-viewer controls and messages, reset confirmations, saved-case picker, and individual and relationship lists. Filter counters update immediately on language changes without altering family data.
helpData.changelog.v1_0_5_rc7.text: Clinical summaries and relationship menus in the tooltip are localized, together with automatically generated fetal, gestational-carrier and donor labels in QC. User-entered data remain unchanged.
helpData.changelog.v1_0_5_rc8.text: Global internationalization review: contextual QC terms in missing-reference and repeated-relation warnings are localized. Documented strict auditing added, with no changes to pedigree layout or JSON schema.
helpData.intro: User guide to the symbols, relationships and conventions implemented in PedigrAPP. The application follows standardized pedigree nomenclature published by the National Society of Genetic Counselors (NSGC), including the subsequent revisions and corrections listed in the references.
helpData.layoutRules.0: Generations use Roman numerals (I, II, III…). Individuals within a generation are numbered when pedigree numbering is enabled.
helpData.layoutRules.1: If parents are added above an individual in Generation I, PedigrAPP inserts a new Generation I and shifts the existing pedigree down a generation without changing its relative structure.
helpData.layoutRules.2: Siblings are placed from left to right by birth/pregnancy order where possible.
helpData.layoutRules.3: When feasible without introducing additional crossings, the man is placed on the left and the woman on the right within a couple.
helpData.layoutRules.4: Multiple unions are arranged to preserve sibships and families of origin as blocks.
helpData.layoutRules.5: Unavoidable crossings may be marked with a small bridge to show that the lines intersect without being connected.
helpData.layoutRules.6: Manual generation or position overrides should be exceptions, for complex pedigrees that cannot be represented adequately by automatic layout.
helpData.notes.0: Where the 2025 correction amends or clarifies the 2022 publication, PedigrAPP follows the corrected 2025 recommendation.
helpData.notes.1: Some symbols and layout choices are application-specific conventions intended to keep pedigrees readable; these are explicitly identified as “PedigrAPP convention”.
helpData.quickStart.0.text: Quick-create shortcuts appear in a card above the viewer, including Father + mother + fetus (P, sex unknown). This can represent a basic prenatal trio without automatically assigning a clinical indication or fetal result. A second card contains the main actions: new family, reset, undo/redo, save, import/export, PDF and help. Below the viewer, Add individual, Advanced relationships and Lists form an accordion. The individual form is arranged in two main rows for readability.
helpData.quickStart.0.title: Add individuals
helpData.quickStart.1.text: Click an individual’s symbol to open its context card. Use it to edit basic details or apply shortcuts such as deceased, proband, consultand or simple affected status.
helpData.quickStart.1.title: Open an individual’s menu
helpData.quickStart.2.text: Select Clinical and genetic information from the context card. Record condition-specific statuses, molecular results, variants, zygosity and comments in the side panel.
helpData.quickStart.2.title: Clinical and genetic information
helpData.quickStart.3.text: For a pregnancy or offspring, open Advanced options and select up to two intended parents. PedigrAPP places their pedigree numbers beneath the symbol and updates them when numbering changes; it does not draw a genetic-parentage line. This clarifies intended parentage, separately from gamete-donor D and gestational-carrier G lines in Bennett 2025.
helpData.quickStart.3.title: Intended parents
helpData.quickStart.4.text: Click a couple’s union line. Under Ended relationship and Consanguineous relationship, choose Reproductive status. Select No offspring by choice / unknown reason or Infertility, attribute it to the couple or an individual, optionally record the reason and save. The one- or two-bar indicator appears automatically. These settings are also available under Advanced relationships.
helpData.quickStart.4.title: Reproductive status of a couple
helpData.quickStart.5.text: Use the tooltip shortcuts for common relationships, including Add fetus and Add stillbirth (SB), both initially with unknown sex. When the selected individual has multiple partners, the shortcut records only that individual as parent; the other parent can be specified later using Advanced relationships. That panel also supports adoption, specific parentage, twins and less common cases.
helpData.quickStart.5.title: Create relationships
helpData.quickStart.6.text: The viewer supports zoom, pan, fit to width, fit whole pedigree and searching for individuals. On loading, the pedigree fits the viewer width. Drag an individual horizontally to adjust their position: connections update and neighbours make room. A short click still opens the context card. Position edits can be saved and undone; ↺ resets manual positions. The ⇄ mode allows rearranging individuals within their generation, including between sibships or donors. Couples and twins move as units without changing recorded parentage or birth order. QC may report inconsistent displayed birth order.
helpData.quickStart.6.title: Navigate the pedigree
helpData.quickStart.7.text: The live QC indicator changes colour as you edit: red for errors, amber for warnings, blue for information, green when no issues are detected and grey for an empty or unchecked pedigree. A violet marker signals graphical issues. Click the indicator to inspect details; the panel stays closed by default. QC does not alter the pedigree and is not a clinical review.
helpData.quickStart.7.title: Live quality control (QC)
helpData.quickStart.8.text: Save cases; import/export JSON and PED; export SVG/PNG; and generate a clinical PDF in the browser.
helpData.quickStart.8.title: Save and export
helpData.relationships.adoption_in.text: The individual is enclosed in brackets. Adoptive parentage is dashed; biological parentage remains solid if shown.
helpData.relationships.adoption_in.title: Adopted into the family
helpData.relationships.adoption_out.text: The individual is enclosed in brackets and retains a solid biological descent line to the family of origin.
helpData.relationships.consanguinity.tex: A double line between the partners. If degree is not apparent, it may be noted as text.
helpData.relationships.ended_union.text: Two slashes (//) mark a relationship that has ended. PedigrAPP does not graphically distinguish separation and divorce.
helpData.relationships.ended_union.title: Ended relationship
helpData.relationships.infertility.text: No-offspring mark with a second bar; PedigrAPP allows recording a reason when known.
helpData.relationships.infertility.title: Infertility
helpData.relationships.intergenerational: PedigrAPP retains both generations and connects the couple with a direct diagonal, avoiding relocation of the rest of the pedigree.
helpData.relationships.multiple_unions.t: Multiple partners are treated as blocks to reduce crossings while keeping sibships and families of origin coherent.
helpData.relationships.no_children.text: A mark below an individual or union indicates no offspring by choice or for an unknown reason. An explanation may be added.
helpData.relationships.no_children.title: No offspring
helpData.relationships.parentage.text: Solid descent line from a couple or parent to a sibship or an individual.
helpData.relationships.parentage.title: Biological parentage
helpData.relationships.sibship.text: Siblings share a horizontal line. The application tries to place them left to right in birth order.
helpData.relationships.sibship.title: Sibship
helpData.relationships.triplets.text: Three or more lines branch from a shared point. PedigrAPP supports trizygotic representation and known zygosity.
helpData.relationships.triplets.title: Triplets / multiples
helpData.relationships.twins.text: Lines originate at a shared point. A connecting bar indicates monozygosity; without it, dizygosity or unspecified zygosity is indicated as appropriate.
helpData.relationships.twins.title: Twins
helpData.relationships.union.text: Horizontal line between two individuals of the same generation.
helpData.relationships.union.title: Couple / relationship
helpData.symbolGroups.conditions.items.c: PedigrAPP depicts carrier status with a condition-specific texture/pattern instead of the former central dot, which the 2022 review discourages as a universal carrier marker.
helpData.symbolGroups.conditions.items.d: The application can mark that the condition-specific assessment is documented. This is a clinical annotation within PedigrAPP.
helpData.symbolGroups.conditions.items.m: For three or more conditions, PedigrAPP allocates radial sectors in a stable clockwise order starting at 12 o’clock. A sector may remain unfilled if the individual does not have that condition.
helpData.symbolGroups.conditions.items.t: For one or two conditions, PedigrAPP uses simple subdivisions of the symbol. The legend identifies each condition by its colour/pattern.
helpData.symbolGroups.conditions.title: Conditions, affected status and carriers
Shading indicates clinical affected status. When conditions are defined, affected status is shown for each condition and explained in the legend.
An arrow points to the person seeking or receiving genetic counselling/testing. PedigrAPP supports more than one consultand.
A diagonal slash crosses the symbol. A cross is avoided to prevent confusion with other annotations.
Diamond. Used when gender is unknown, irrelevant or not represented as man/woman. PedigrAPP can additionally record AMAB, AFAB or UAAB.
A “?” associated with an individual indicates insufficient information on their family history.
Circle. Sex assigned at birth is documented separately when relevant.
Square. In the 2022 review and 2025 correction, shape denotes gender identity. Sex assigned at birth is recorded separately.
The number appears inside the symbol. Affected individuals who need to be distinguished should not be grouped.
An “n” is shown inside the symbol when the number is unknown or unspecified.
An arrow accompanied by “P”. PedigrAPP maintains only one active proband in each pedigree.
helpData.symbolGroups.individuals.title: Individual symbols
helpData.symbolGroups.pregnancy.items.ec: Triangle with the ECT mark. The 2025 correction reinstates the diagonal slash accidentally omitted from the 2022 figure.
helpData.symbolGroups.pregnancy.items.fe: PedigrAPP uses a specific symbol with “P” and allows recording fetal sex and gestational age.
helpData.symbolGroups.pregnancy.items.sa: Triangle for a pregnancy that did not reach term, labelled SAB.
helpData.symbolGroups.pregnancy.items.st: Symbol for an individual who died in association with pregnancy; gestational age may be recorded.
helpData.symbolGroups.pregnancy.items.to: Triangle for a termination of pregnancy, labelled TOP.
helpData.symbolGroups.pregnancy.title: Pregnancy and pregnancy loss
helpData.symbolGroups.reproduction.items: “D” denotes a gamete donor where appropriate. PedigrAPP distinguishes sperm from egg donation by the relationship to the resulting pregnancy or offspring.
“G” identifies a person carrying a pregnancy from a preimplantation embryo without contributing genetic material to that embryo.
Strictly, the surrogate supplies the egg and carries the pregnancy. PedigrAPP uses the donor “D” convention and directly links the gestation; it does not use a dedicated “S” symbol.
Surrogate: egg donor and gestational carrier

helpData.tooltip.0: Click an individual to open the context card. Simply hovering does not open it.
helpData.tooltip.1: Quick fields let you modify the name/alias, brief information and auxiliary data allowed for the record type.
helpData.tooltip.2: The lower icons let you edit, change gender/sex, mark deceased, proband, consultand and simple affected status, as well as other contextual actions.
helpData.tooltip.3: The prominent Clinical and genetic information button selects the individual and opens the clinical panel.
helpData.tooltip.4: The Clinical and genetic information panel is available for individuals, fetuses, stillbirths, SAB, TOP, ECT, donors and gestational carriers. It opens as an overlay on the right, with the pedigree still visible. Its header keeps the selected record visible and lets you move through records in visual generation/position order. The context card groups identity, status, clinical access, family shortcuts, clinical summary, advanced options and edit/delete. When the top actions scroll out of view, a compact fixed bar appears for Undo, Redo, Save and Back to pedigree. Add individual, Advanced relationships and Lists form an accordion. Keyboard shortcuts include Ctrl/Cmd+S to save, Ctrl/Cmd+Z to undo, Ctrl/Cmd+Y or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z to redo, F for search, +/- for zoom and Esc to close panels or focus mode. Confirmation toasts appear temporarily in the bottom-right corner; errors remain visible in the message area. Cases can be marked reviewed, and the reviewed status is saved with the pedigree. The saved-case chooser supports All, Reviewed and Not reviewed filters. Multiple-individual groups may contain clinical comments, but do not have one shared condition-specific clinical status.
helpData.tooltip.5: The “⋯” menu contains less frequently used actions, including manual positioning and relationships between existing individuals.

legend.adoption.brackets: In adoption, the individual is shown in brackets. Adopted in connects to adoptive parents by a dashed line; Adopted out retains a solid biological parentage line.
legend.comment.dot: The comment dot is a UI indicator and is not part of pedigree nomenclature.
legend.condition.sectors: Each sector represents a condition–status combination. The patterns for Affected and Unaffected carrier are explicitly defined and must be distinct.
legend.condition.unknown: An unfilled symbol with “?” is an application convention indicating unknown or undocumented condition status.
legend.condition.zygosity: Sector size does not represent zygosity; homozygosity, heterozygosity, hemizygosity and heteroplasmy are documented in the molecular record.
legend.pregnancy.affected: In affected pregnancy events, the triangle uses the fill or pattern associated with the condition.
legend.relationship.ended: Two diagonal slashes (//) across a couple line indicate an ended relationship.
legend.surrogate.egg: Surrogate: the person provides the egg and carries the pregnancy. She is represented by D, with the outcome directly below on a solid line.

helpData.changelog.v1_0_6.text: Version 1.0.6 introduces mutually exclusive age or birth year in the tooltip and full form, shown as b. YYYY. Donor and gestational-carrier records can form explicit unions without automatically implying biological parentage; gestational events cannot be partners.
help.gestation.explicitAssignment: Select one outcome. Person A must have female sex assigned at birth (AFAB), regardless of gender. This does not create genetic parentage or a partnership.
validation.gestation.afabRequired: Explicit gestation requires a person assigned female at birth (AFAB).
validation.gestation.outcomeRequired: Select a valid reproductive outcome other than the gestating person.
validation.gestation.carrierConflict: This outcome already has a gestational carrier (G) or surrogate. Gestation cannot be assigned twice.
validation.gestation.duplicate: Each outcome can have only one explicit gestation assignment.
helpData.changelog.v1_0_6_rc2.text: Adds explicit gestation assignment from Advanced relationships or More (…) for people assigned female at birth (AFAB), including transgender men, following figure 5.1.d in the Bennett (2025) correction. Gestation lines originate from the assigned individual without implying that their partner carried the pregnancy or that gestation establishes genetic parentage.
validation.gestation.cycle: This gestation assignment would create a cycle with the recorded parentage.
help.sharedDonor.advanced: Select the children, fetuses, or pregnancy outcomes linked to the same donor. Existing links are checked; uncheck to unlink. Sibling relationships and parentage are not changed.

helpData.changelog.v1_0_6_rc3.text: An existing sperm or egg donor can be linked to multiple outcomes through Advanced relationships or ⋯ More. Siblings retain one shared sibling bar and a single D; partnerships and parentage are not created automatically.
help.sharedDonor.fromRecipient: Select one existing sperm or egg donor. This individual will be added to the donor’s linked outcomes; sibling relationships and parentage will remain unchanged.
validation.sharedDonor.chooseOneDonor: Select exactly one existing donor for this individual.
message.sharedDonor.linked: Existing donor linked without changing the sibling group.
helpData.changelog.v1_1.text: Stable version 1.1 consolidates the 1.0.6 development line: mutually exclusive age or birth year, partnerships involving donors and gestational carriers, explicit pregnancy gestation assignment to people assigned female at birth regardless of gender (2025 correction, Fig. 5.1.d), and sperm/egg donor reuse across several offspring while preserving sibling groups (Fig. 5.1.c). Existing records remain compatible; JSON schema stays at 4.19.
